data.body:
Second occurrence observed 2026-05-30 (variant: --resume creates DUPLICATE PR rather than erroring).

Repro path:
1. ran .claude/scripts/dso merge-to-main.sh on branch fix-g2-and-pr482-nits → created staged-6fc8b2284d4e-1780175083 + PR #490. Exit 0. Auto-merge pending on PR #490 (CI checks running).
2. While #490 was still pending, ran .claude/scripts/dso merge-to-main.sh --resume → created staged-6fc8b2284d4e-1780176147 + PR #492 (different timestamp suffix, same source branch, same diff). Exit 0.

Outcome: two open PR1s referencing the same source branch, each pointing at a different staged-* ref. Distinct from the originally-filed symptom where both invocations error "non-draft PR already exists" — here --resume bypassed the existing-PR guard entirely, possibly because of a stale or missing checkpoint file.

Hypothesis: there are TWO related defects (or one with two manifestations):
  (a) the existing-PR guard fires when checkpoint state EXISTS (gives "already exists" error) — the originally-filed symptom on PR #491
  (b) when checkpoint state does NOT exist (e.g., never written, or cleaned up between runs), the script falls through to fresh-PR-creation and produces a duplicate — the new symptom on PR #490/#492

Workaround applied: closed PR #492 via gh + deleted its staged ref.

Suggested fix scope expansion: detect existing open PR1 for the same source branch BEFORE attempting staged-ref creation, independent of checkpoint state. The check should be authoritative from gh API state, not from local checkpoint.
